teaser: RiskMandate and the Agent Behaviour Policy in plain words: what it does, why it is not real time, which agents it covers, and how it gets into the room.
core_idea: An Agent Behaviour Policy writes down, for one agent in one deployment, what it can reach, what was authorised, the gap and the barrier on each capability; RiskMandate stays out of the request path so runtimes can enforce it, has policies for commercial agents from vendor pages and measurement, names the enterprise-assistant oversharing risk as the gap, and gets into the room through questions already being asked.

quotes.text: They are precise, and precision is not the same as clear.
The policy is the description; the runtime is the enforcer; the barrier column says which rules have one.
The common thread is that none of these asks anyone to understand agents first.
